_comment: gobj-ui declarative-shell demo. One primary menu (menu.primary) rendered as a VERTICAL rail on desktop (left) and an ICON-BAR on mobile (bottom) — that single pair already shows the per-zone responsive model. Each primary item is a chapter that demonstrates one SECONDARY layout in the content column: TABS (top-sub), SIDE SUBMENU (right), CARDS section-index + mobile BACKBAR, and a right-zone VERTICAL submenu. The toolbar burger opens a DRAWER (off-canvas vertical). The Accordion chapter has a direct target whose view embeds a live accordion nav (accordion is a primary-zone layout: its section bodies are the routable 2nd-level items, so it can't be a 3rd-level submenu). Every leaf mounts C_TEST_VIEW, which names on screen exactly which layout(s) are visible and where.

routes._sitemap_comment: Action route (ROUTING.md 7.1): fires EV_OPEN_SITEMAP instead of mounting a view. redirect:'back' because the site map is a floating C_YUI_WINDOW on the overlay stack (no opener-owned URL hook, so 'stay' would leave the URL stale on close).
routes._prefs_comment: The OTHER action-route flavour, and the reason it is here: redirect:'stay' keeps the URL on /prefs so the modal is deep-linkable, which means current_route stays on the resting view while the URL sits off it. That divergence is what the overlay/history bookkeeping has to survive (Back must still close the modal), and 'back' does not exercise it. Per ROUTING.md 7.1 'stay' is only correct when the opener owns the URL on close: ac_open_prefs' on_close does the history.back(), wattyzer's open_route_modal idiom.

items.tooltip: Open the off-canvas drawer (a menu rendered with layout:"drawer")

items.name: ES/EN
items.tooltip: Switch language (English / Spanish)
Toggle light / dark (Bulma data-theme)

items.name: Go to Meter 1 · series
items._comment: A SHORTCUT: a non-structural edge that simply navigates to a canonical path. It reaches four levels into the node tree AND two into the data space below the link, with no declaration of those levels anywhere — the url is the whole contract. Note what a shortcut is NOT: it does not know whether its target still exists, so if that node is removed the tree lands the user on the nearest living ancestor and logs it.

primary._comment: Rendered VERTICAL in the left rail (desktop) and as an ICON-BAR in the bottom bar (mobile) — same items, two zones, no duplication. This is layouts #1 (vertical) and #2 (icon-bar).

items.name: Tabs
items.tooltip: Secondary nav as a horizontal tab strip (top-sub)

kw.title: Tabs — Tab A
kw.lead: The secondary nav above is layout "tabs": a Bulma .tabs strip in the top-sub zone. Tab strips have no room for section headers, so decorative header/divider items are silently dropped here.

kw.title: Tabs — Tab B
kw.lead: Same tab strip; a different leaf mounted in the main stage. keep_alive: switch tabs and come back — the instance number below does not change.

kw.title: Tabs — Tab C
kw.lead: This leaf is lazy_destroy: leave it and it is destroyed; return and the instance number below has incremented (a fresh gobj was built).

items.name: Side submenu
items.tooltip: Secondary nav as a titled vertical list on the right

kw.title: Side submenu — Profile
kw.lead: The right-hand list is layout "submenu": a Bulma .menu with a heading. Unlike tabs, it renders decorative type:"header" and type:"divider" items — see the "Account" / "Security" group labels.

kw.title: Side submenu — Sessions
kw.lead: Grouping without a third nav level: header + divider items chunk the list visually while the route tree stays two levels deep.

kw.title: Side submenu — Tokens
kw.lead: On mobile the right zone is hidden (show_on ">=desktop") — resize the window narrow and this secondary nav collapses; the primary icon-bar at the bottom takes over.

items.name: Cards
items.tooltip: A tree of node gobjs: cards inside cards, any depth
items._comment: PROTOTYPE of the node-tree model (C_YUI_NODE). ONE declared route: the shell resolves /cards and hands the tree everything below as a subpath, so depth is unbounded and no route table grows. A node is a gobj, the gobj tree IS the navigation tree, and each node holds HOW IT WANTS ITS CHILDREN SEEN (projection). The declared `children` below are not a privileged path: mt_create feeds them to the same EV_ADD_NODE the runtime API uses — see the buttons in the panel at /cards.

kw.title: Node tree
kw.lead: The cards below are child NODES, each a gobj. Walk in: Energy → North hall → Meter 1 is four levels deep on one declared route. The buttons reshape the LIVE tree through the same API the config used at boot.

kw.title: Cards — Alpha
kw.lead: A leaf directly under the root: a node with content and no children. The route #/cards/alpha is unchanged from the old section-index demo.

kw.title: Cards — Beta
kw.lead: This node has CONTENT and CHILDREN at the same time: the content is the page, the children are projected under it. One node, not two concepts.

kw.title: Beta one
kw.lead: Reached from a card under Beta's own content.

kw.title: Beta two
kw.lead: Back returns to Beta, which shows its content again.

children.label: North hall
Meter 1
children._link_comment: WHERE THE TREE ENDS. This node does not branch: it LINKS to a data space (a timeranger: millions of raw records, series/time, key/value) and mounts the viewer suited to it. Everything below in the url — #/cards/energy/north/m1/series/kwh_total — is handed to that viewer as EV_ROUTE_CHANGED {base, subpath}, the same contract the shell gives a view. One gobj per structural node is right; one gobj per record is not.

children.label: Meter 2
children._link_comment: WHERE THE TREE ENDS. This node does not branch: it LINKS to a data space (a timeranger: millions of raw records, series/time, key/value) and mounts the viewer suited to it. Everything below in the url — #/cards/energy/north/m1/series/kwh_total — is handed to that viewer as EV_ROUTE_CHANGED {base, subpath}, the same contract the shell gives a view. One gobj per structural node is right; one gobj per record is not.

children._aliases_comment: This node used to be called 'hall1'. The tree's paths are a CONTRACT — urls a client may hold — so the id was not rewritten in place: #/cards/energy/hall1/m1 still resolves and is rewritten (replace) to the canonical spelling. That is what a version bump migrates through; there is no reparent API on purpose.

children.label: South hall

kw.title: Meter 3
kw.lead: Same depth as Meter 1, but this branch declares chrome_depth: 1, so only ONE chrome strip is painted instead of one per ancestor. How much chrome a corner of the tree deserves is a property of the tree, not of the renderer.

children._chrome_depth_comment: Cap the stacked chrome for THIS branch: only the strip nearest the tip is painted, instead of one per ancestor. The deepest declaration on the path wins, so an intermediate node whose only job is to hold this number is a legitimate node. Compare #/cards/energy/south/m3 (one strip) with #/cards/energy/north/m1 (three).

kw.title: Tank 1
kw.lead: Its parent projects its children as a VERTICAL list instead of cards. Same tree, same URLs — a projection is HOW you see the children, not WHERE you are.

kw.title: Tank 2
kw.lead: Change the projection from the panel at /cards and watch the shape change without the URL moving.

items.name: Section index
items.tooltip: The shell's own submenu.index landing (two levels)

submenu._comment: index:true turns /cards into a real, deep-linkable landing rendered as a CARDS grid (a synthesized C_YUI_NAV, layout:"cards"). Tabs and cards never coexist: the tab strip defaults to >=tablet, and on mobile a BACKBAR (< Cards) replaces it inside each child view.

kw.title: Section index — Alpha
kw.lead: The SHELL synthesized this landing from submenu.index: one card per submenu item, capped at two levels (primary nav + submenu). Compare with the Cards chapter, where the same look comes from a recursive tree of node gobjs.

kw.title: Section index — Beta
kw.lead: submenu.index is the shipped mechanism wattyzer uses for /reports. It stays here because it is what five apps run in production today.

kw.title: Section index — Gamma
kw.lead: Two levels is all this mechanism has: a submenu item cannot declare a submenu of its own.

kw.title: Section index — Delta
kw.lead: For arbitrary depth, see the Cards chapter (C_YUI_NODE).

items.name: Accordion
items.tooltip: Collapsible groups — a primary-zone layout, shown here as a live illustration

kw.title: Accordion
kw.lead: Accordion is a PRIMARY-zone layout: its first-level entries are collapsible sections and their bodies are the second-level items. Because those bodies are the routable 2nd level, accordion can't be a 3rd-level submenu — so this chapter embeds a live accordion nav below. Click a section head to expand; click a leaf to navigate for real.

items.name: Form
items.tooltip: A real C_YUI_FORM component: editable fields + save/undo toolbar

kw.title: Form
kw.lead: This is the gobj-ui form component C_YUI_FORM, hosted as a child. The template here is a catalogue of every field type the component can render — text, email, url, tel, password, integer, real, percent, currency, color, datetime, coordinates, checkbox, a native enum select and a multi-select (TomSelect). Edit any value and press Save (floppy icon) — the component publishes EV_SAVE_RECORD and the submitted JSON appears below.

items.name: Table
items.tooltip: A real Tabulator data table with sortable columns

kw.title: Table
kw.lead: A Tabulator data table with static rows, built directly in the view (the pattern the yunos use, e.g. gui_agent's node list). Click a header to sort, click a row to select; the Status column uses a coloured-tag formatter.

items.name: TreeDB
items.tooltip: A treedb topic table whose edit dialog hosts C_YUI_FORM

kw.title: TreeDB
kw.lead: The real C_YUI_TREEDB_TOPIC_WITH_FORM against an in-memory backend (this view answers get_topic_data and echoes the published record events). Press EDIT, then a row's pen icon — the dialog is a hosted C_YUI_FORM: readonly pkey on update, fkey TomSelects fed with sibling-topic rows, a raw-JSON editor for the dict col, and the form's own bottom toolbar as dialog footer. NEW opens the same form in create mode.

items.name: Chart
items.tooltip: A uPlot time-series chart

kw.title: Chart
kw.lead: The gobj-ui uPlot component C_YUI_UPLOT. Series are added with EV_ADD_SERIE and rows fed with EV_LOAD_DATA (a unix-epoch-seconds x-axis). Hover to read values; drag to zoom. Fully offline.

items.name: Frontend view
items.tooltip: The live gobj tree of this very yuno (G6)

kw.title: Frontend view
kw.lead: C_YUI_GOBJ_TREE_JS introspects the running yuno and draws its live gobj tree with G6 — self-referential: you see the yuno, this view and the tree component itself. Use the toolbar to zoom, center, and expand/collapse. No data, no backend.

items.name: JSON graph
items.tooltip: Any JSON value as a hierarchical G6 graph

kw.title: JSON graph
kw.lead: C_YUI_JSON_GRAPH renders an arbitrary JSON value as a hierarchical graph (objects/arrays as group nodes, scalars as rows). Click a node to emit EV_JSON_ITEM_CLICKED. Fully offline.

items.name: JSON tree
items.tooltip: C_YUI_JSON: the lazy JSON tree viewer

kw.title: JSON tree
kw.lead: C_YUI_JSON renders a value as a lazily expanded tree. Indentation is four characters per level and each ancestor draws a guide line, the same as the site map: past level two the eye follows the guide, not the offset.

items.name: Wizard
items.tooltip: A multi-step wizard (Back / Next / Confirm)

kw.title: Wizard
kw.lead: C_YUI_WIZARD walks ordered steps with a title + "N / M" counter + Back/Next, turning into Confirm on the last step. Steps are fed with EV_SET_STEPS; Confirm publishes EV_WIZARD_DONE (echoed below the wizard). Fully offline.

items.name: Pager
items.tooltip: A drill-down page stack (← back)

kw.title: Pager
kw.lead: C_YUI_PAGER stacks panels with a "← title" header (drill-down, no confirm chrome). Push a page with the button, pop back with the header "←". Pages here are plain content; a real one would push a C_YUI_FORM. Fully offline.

items.name: Period
items.tooltip: The date navigator: granularity + arrows + calendar

kw.title: Period
kw.lead: C_YUI_PERIOD is a date navigator: pick a granularity, then walk it with the arrows (the label opens a calendar). A period is not an enum — it is (unit, count) — so the SAME component gives quarters, semesters, bimesters or 15-minute buckets by declaring them. Two instances below with different sets; every EV_PERIOD_CHANGED is echoed with the timestamps the bucket resolves to. Fully offline.

items.name: Modals
items.tooltip: Shell confirm/notification helpers

kw.title: Modals
kw.lead: The shell modal helpers (shell_modals.js): Promise-based icon-centric confirms (yui_shell_confirm_ok / yesno / yesnocancel) on the shell's modal layer riding its Escape priority chain — Enter answers the primary, Escape dismisses with the safe default, repeat presses never stack a second modal — and auto-dismiss notifications (yui_shell_show_info / warning / error). Each answer is echoed below the buttons. Fully offline.

items.name: Windows
items.tooltip: Floating C_YUI_WINDOWs + the C_YUI_WINDOW_MANAGER dock

kw.title: Windows
kw.lead: C_YUI_WINDOW floating windows managed by the C_YUI_WINDOW_MANAGER dock (service __window_manager__). Spawn a few: drag the titlebar, resize the edges, maximize; minimize rolls a window to a chip in the dock strip below, a press raises/focuses it, x closes it. Open windows float over the other chapters (the view is keep_alive). On mobile a window becomes a full-screen sheet — minimize it to the dock to get back. Fully offline.

items.name: Map
items.tooltip: A MapLibre map with markers (needs network)

kw.title: Map
kw.lead: C_YUI_MAP (MapLibre) rendered into an external sized element, with a few Spanish cities as markers. NOTE: the basemap tiles come from tiles.openfreemap.org, so this chapter needs network; offline it shows a blank map with controls.

quick._comment: A menu rendered with layout:"drawer": an off-canvas panel on the overlay layer (its inner list reuses the vertical renderer). Opened by the toolbar burger. Items carry only a route and no target, so they resolve to the same route-index entries as the primary menu — no duplicate view gobjs.
